enquiry: We run a cell culture process in an aqueous medium. Glucose and lactate are measured from samples, and the delay makes it difficult to see changes promptly. We are exploring an in situ spectroscopy pilot that can be checked against those existing laboratory measurements. The medium and cell population change during the run; we have not yet selected a probe or a calibration strategy.

items.finding: Combining inputs using low-level data fusion rearranges data from different sources into a new matrix where variables are placed one after another.
items.how_it_applies: This approach could be tested when combining Raman and MIR datasets for a multi-method setup, provided the individual datasets show sufficient complementarity.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: Published food analytical studies show that instrument complementarity is not always sufficient to improve predictive performance, so this must be validated on the actual cell culture matrix.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
